answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a licensed solar-mirror field on a named dune: the holder tends one heliostat array whose reflected beam is logged by an independent solar receiver, and random live checks demand the operator tilt that exact mirror to flash an echo of light back to the verifier within minutes, which one person cannot do from two fields at once. The license fee in outside money doubles per further field on the same funding trail, so each extra fake identity costs another real mirror array, another dune lease, another live operator, and twice the prior fee.
